title: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 11](/bible/1-kings/11)

**[1 Kings 11:1-3](/bible/1-kings/11#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/11#v1)</sup> But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/11#v2)</sup> Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/11#v3)</sup> And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.

- Solomon loved many strange women besides the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites, nations the Most High had said Israel should not join with, for surely they would turn their heart after their gods; and Solomon clave to these in love.
- He had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned away his heart. It happened exactly as the Most High said it would, for the law had warned that intermarriage would turn the heart to serve other gods, and it was not a maybe but a will.

  Precepts:
  - **[Deuteronomy 7:3](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)</sup> Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.

    Make no marriages with the other nations, for they will turn away thy son from following the Most High.
  - **[Exodus 34:16](/bible/exodus/34#v16)**
    > <sup>[16](/bible/exodus/34#v16)</sup> And thou take of their daughters unto thy sons, and their daughters go a whoring after their gods, and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.

    Their daughters will go a whoring after their gods and make thy sons go a whoring after their gods.
  - **[Deuteronomy 17:17](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v17)**
    > <sup>[17](/bible/deuteronomy/17#v17)</sup> Neither shall he multiply wives to himself, that his heart turn not away: neither shall he greatly multiply to himself silver and gold.

    The king shall not multiply wives to himself, nor greatly multiply silver and gold, which is exactly what Solomon did.

**[1 Kings 11:4-8](/bible/1-kings/11#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/11#v4)</sup> For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/11#v5)</sup> For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/11#v6)</sup> And Solomon did evil in the sight of the Lord, and went not fully after the Lord, as did David his father.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/11#v7)</sup> Then did Solomon build an high place for Chemosh, the abomination of Moab, in the hill that is before Jerusalem, and for Molech, the abomination of the children of Ammon.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/11#v8)</sup> And likewise did he for all his strange wives, which burnt incense and sacrificed unto their gods.

- When Solomon was old his wives turned his heart after other gods, and his heart was not perfect with the Most High as David his father's was; he went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians and Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites, and did evil in the sight of the Most High.
- David also sinned, but when David sinned he repented and turned back, while Solomon kept going into sin; this is why a righteous man falls seven times and rises again.
- Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

  Precepts:
  - **[Amos 5:26](/bible/amos/5#v26)**
    > <sup>[26](/bible/amos/5#v26)</sup> But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.

    Israel bore the tabernacle of Molech and the star of their god, the six-pointed star that came from the idolatry of Solomon's day.
  - **[Acts 7:43](/bible/acts/7#v43)**
    > <sup>[43](/bible/acts/7#v43)</sup> Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.

    Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles, the same idol.

**[1 Kings 11:9-13](/bible/1-kings/11#v9)**

> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/11#v9)</sup> And the Lord was angry with Solomon, because his heart was turned from the Lord God of Israel, which had appeared unto him twice,
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/11#v10)</sup> And had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods: but he kept not that which the Lord commanded.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/11#v11)</sup> Wherefore the Lord said unto Solomon, Forasmuch as this is done of thee, and thou hast not kept my covenant and my statutes, which I have commanded thee, I will surely rend the kingdom from thee, and will give it to thy servant.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/11#v12)</sup> Notwithstanding in thy days I will not do it for David thy father’s sake: but I will rend it out of the hand of thy son.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/11#v13)</sup> Howbeit I will not rend away all the kingdom; but will give one tribe to thy son for David my servant’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake which I have chosen.

- The Most High was angry with Solomon because his heart was turned from him who had appeared to him twice and commanded him not to go after other gods, but he kept not the commandment.
- Therefore the Most High said he would surely rend the kingdom from Solomon and give it to his servant, but not in Solomon's days for David's sake; he would rend it out of the hand of his son.
- This is the pivotal moment in the history of Israel, for this sin divided the kingdom under Jeroboam and Rehoboam. The Most High said he would not rend all the kingdom but would give one tribe to the son of David for David's sake and for Jerusalem's sake.

**[1 Kings 11:14-25](/bible/1-kings/11#v14)**

> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/11#v14)</sup> And the Lord stirred up an adversary unto Solomon, Hadad the Edomite: he was of the king’s seed in Edom.
>
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/11#v15)</sup> For it came to pass, when David was in Edom, and Joab the captain of the host was gone up to bury the slain, after he had smitten every male in Edom;
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/11#v16)</sup> (For six months did Joab remain there with all Israel, until he had cut off every male in Edom:)
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/11#v17)</sup> That Hadad fled, he and certain Edomites of his father’s servants with him, to go into Egypt; Hadad being yet a little child.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/11#v18)</sup> And they arose out of Midian, and came to Paran: and they took men with them out of Paran, and they came to Egypt, unto Pharaoh king of Egypt; which gave him an house, and appointed him victuals, and gave him land.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/11#v19)</sup> And Hadad found great favour in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him to wife the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/11#v20)</sup> And the sister of Tahpenes bare him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh’s house: and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s household among the sons of Pharaoh.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/11#v21)</sup> And when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers, and that Joab the captain of the host was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, Let me depart, that I may go to mine own country.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/11#v22)</sup> Then Pharaoh said unto him, But what hast thou lacked with me, that, behold, thou seekest to go to thine own country? And he answered, Nothing: howbeit let me go in any wise.
>
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/11#v23)</sup> And God stirred him up another adversary, Rezon the son of Eliadah, which fled from his lord Hadadezer king of Zobah:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/11#v24)</sup> And he gathered men unto him, and became captain over a band, when David slew them of Zobah: and they went to Damascus, and dwelt therein, and reigned in Damascus.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/11#v25)</sup> And he was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon, beside the mischief that Hadad did: and he abhorred Israel, and reigned over Syria.

- The Most High stirred up an adversary to Solomon, Hadad the Edomite, of the king's seed in Edom, for when David was in Edom, Joab remained six months until he had cut off every male, and Hadad fled as a child to Egypt where Pharaoh gave him favor, a house, and a wife.
- Esau was always the first hater and enemy of Israel, comforting himself in the thought of killing us. When Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he sought to return to his own country.
- The Most High also stirred up Rezin the son of Eliadah, who gathered men, reigned in Damascus, and was an adversary to Israel all the days of Solomon. There was peace under Solomon while he kept the commandments, but when he broke them the Most High gave strength to his enemies.

**[1 Kings 11:26-40](/bible/1-kings/11#v26)**

> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/11#v26)</sup> And Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephrathite of Zereda, Solomon’s servant, whose mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow woman, even he lifted up his hand against the king.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/11#v27)</sup> And this was the cause that he lifted up his hand against the king: Solomon built Millo, and repaired the breaches of the city of David his father.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/11#v28)</sup> And the man Jeroboam was a mighty man of valour: and Solomon seeing the young man that he was industrious, he made him ruler over all the charge of the house of Joseph.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/11#v29)</sup> And it came to pass at that time when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, that the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him in the way; and he had clad himself with a new garment; and they two were alone in the field:
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-kings/11#v30)</sup> And Ahijah caught the new garment that was on him, and rent it in twelve pieces:
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-kings/11#v31)</sup> And he said to Jeroboam, Take thee ten pieces: for thus saith the Lord, the God of Israel, Behold, I will rend the kingdom out of the hand of Solomon, and will give ten tribes to thee:
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-kings/11#v32)</sup> (But he shall have one tribe for my servant David’s sake, and for Jerusalem’s sake, the city which I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel:)
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/11#v33)</sup> Because that they have forsaken me, and have worshipped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Zidonians, Chemosh the god of the Moabites, and Milcom the god of the children of Ammon, and have not walked in my ways, to do that which is right in mine eyes, and to keep my statutes and my judgments, as did David his father.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-kings/11#v34)</sup> Howbeit I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand: but I will make him prince all the days of his life for David my servant’s sake, whom I chose, because he kept my commandments and my statutes:
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/1-kings/11#v35)</sup> But I will take the kingdom out of his son’s hand, and will give it unto thee, even ten tribes.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/1-kings/11#v36)</sup> And unto his son will I give one tribe, that David my servant may have a light alway before me in Jerusalem, the city which I have chosen me to put my name there.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/1-kings/11#v37)</sup> And I will take thee, and thou shalt reign according to all that thy soul desireth, and shalt be king over Israel.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/1-kings/11#v38)</sup> And it shall be, if thou wilt hearken unto all that I command thee, and wilt walk in my ways, and do that is right in my sight, to keep my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did; that I will be with thee, and build thee a sure house, as I built for David, and will give Israel unto thee.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/1-kings/11#v39)</sup> And I will for this afflict the seed of David, but not for ever.
>
> <sup>[40](/bible/1-kings/11#v40)</sup> Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. And Jeroboam arose, and fled into Egypt, unto Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.

- Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant, a mighty man of valor, lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon had made him ruler over the charge of the house of Joseph, which was the two tribes Ephraim and Manasseh.
- The prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met Jeroboam in the way, took his new garment, rent it in twelve pieces, and gave Jeroboam ten, saying the Most High would rend ten tribes from Solomon's hand and give them to him. One tribe would remain for David's servant's sake and for Jerusalem, because Israel had forsaken the Most High and worshipped Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom.
- The house of David held Judah and Benjamin, with Levi, so that ten tribes went to Jeroboam. If Jeroboam would walk in the ways of the Most High and keep his statutes, the Most High would build him a sure house as he built for David. Solomon then sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Shishak king of Egypt until Solomon died.

  Precepts:
  - **[Joshua 14:4](/bible/joshua/14#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/joshua/14#v4)</sup> For the children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim: therefore they gave no part unto the Levites in the land, save cities to dwell in, with their suburbs for their cattle and for their substance.

    The children of Joseph were two tribes, Manasseh and Ephraim.
  - **[1 Kings 2:1-4](/bible/1-kings/2#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/2#v1)</sup> Now the days of David drew nigh that he should die; and he charged Solomon his son, saying,
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/2#v2)</sup> I go the way of all the earth: be thou strong therefore, and shew thyself a man;
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/2#v3)</sup> And keep the charge of the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, to keep his statutes, and his commandments, and his judgments, and his testimonies, as it is written in the law of Moses, that thou mayest prosper in all that thou doest, and whithersoever thou turnest thyself:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/2#v4)</sup> That the Lord may continue his word which he spake concerning me, saying, If thy children take heed to their way, to walk before me in truth with all their heart and with all their soul, there shall not fail thee (said he) a man on the throne of Israel.

    David charged Solomon to be strong, show himself a man, and keep the statutes of the Most High as written in the law of Moses.

**[1 Kings 11:41-43](/bible/1-kings/11#v41)**

> <sup>[41](/bible/1-kings/11#v41)</sup> And the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the book of the acts of Solomon?
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/1-kings/11#v42)</sup> And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/1-kings/11#v43)</sup> And Solomon slept with his fathers, and was buried in the city of David his father: and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.

- The rest of the acts of Solomon and his wisdom are written in the book of the acts of Solomon; he reigned in Jerusalem over Israel forty years, then slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David, and Rehoboam his son reigned in his stead.
